title: Multi-LLM Collaboration + Data-Centric Innovation = 2x Better Vulnerability Repair
venue: ICSE 2024 Research Track (published as "Out of Sight, Out of Mind: Better Automatic Vulnerability Repair by Broadening Input Ranges and Sources")
structure_gain: Removing serialized AST sequence drops EM by 1.0pp (20.0%->19.0%); removing CWE knowledge drops it 1.1pp; removing full-function input drops it 1.2pp, all on the same adapted-CodeT5 backbone and training budget
confound_note: Ablation removes one input component at a time (full function / AST / CWE knowledge) while holding backbone (adapted-CodeT5) and training budget fixed, isolating each representation's contribution
threats_to_datum: Assumes perfect fault localization (not realistic deployment); EM metric can penalize semantically-correct but syntactically different patches (Sec 6.5 Threats to Validity)

title: SPVR: syntax-to-prompt vulnerability repair based on large language models
venue: Automated Software Engineering (Springer journal), vol. 33 (2026), article 38

key_numbers.metric: Pass@3 repairs (ChatGPT-4, with vs without SPVR)
Ablation Pass@3 (ChatGPT-3.5-turbo, with vs without MET info)

structure_gain: Removing MET-derived (AST-diff) syntax info dropped pass@3 from 138/547 to 55/547 on ChatGPT-3.5-turbo, same model/samples/metric (Table 10, Sec 5.4) -- roughly 151% relative gain from the structured syntax cues.
confound_note: Ablation in Table 10 holds model and dataset fixed, varying only whether MET-derived syntax info is in the prompt -- a clean representation-only comparison; the headline comparison to VRepair (Table 5) confounds model/architecture and decoding strategy (pass@3 vs beam size 50).
threats_to_datum: C/C++ only; hand-derived extraction rules cover only 61.39% of samples and were mined from under 5% of the dataset (Table 2); correctness judged by string/CodeBLEU match to ground truth, no runtime or semantic verification.

title: Utilizing Precise and Complete Code Context to Guide LLM in Automatic False Positive Mitigation

key_numbers.metric: Juliet F1 (CSA warnings, before vs after)

structure_gain: eCPG-based slicing (vs full-file raw context, LLM4FPM-noslice) improves accuracy by +3.02pp and F1 by +1.73pp on the same Qwen2.5-32B model (Table III); the raw-file variant also fails outright on 40 cases due to context-window overflow.
confound_note: RQ3 ablation (Table III) isolates representation by holding the LLM fixed while toggling eCPG-slicing and FARF; the RQ1 comparison to prior SOTA LLM4SA confounds representation with differing prompting strategy and self-consistency voting.
threats_to_datum: Most real-world false negatives traced to Joern parsing failures (macros, function pointers, #ifdef); slicing granularity is file-level, not function/variable-level; C/C++ only, no cross-language evaluation.

title: Neuro-symbolic Static Analysis with LLM-generated Vulnerability Patterns
datasets: CVE database / GitHub patches (custom curated set)

key_numbers.value: MoCQ 77.4% vs DSL0 (no spec) 9.9% vs DSL100 50.0%
MoCQ 269 TP/197 FP vs Pure LLM 185 TP/182 FP vs Expert queries 222 TP/184 FP

structure_gain: Providing a subset DSL grammar (MoCQ) instead of no specification raises query-generation pass rate from 9.9% (DSL0) to 77.4%, and F1 from 0.31 (DSL100, full grammar) to 0.51 (MoCQ), same LLM loop (Tables 7-8).
confound_note: The DSL0/DSL100/MoCQ ablation varies only the amount/form of structured grammar given to the same iterative LLM loop -- a clean representation-only ablation; the SOTA comparison (Table 4, vs Pure LLM/GRACE/KNighter/IRIS) also changes analysis architecture entirely.
threats_to_datum: Numbers span multiple ablation tables (2, 4, 7, 8) in a still-revised preprint (v5, 2026); CPG/CodeQL backend differs per language, which may confound the cross-language comparison.

title: CognixShield: PoV-Guided Vulnerable API Usage Detection in Large Codebases via LLMs

key_numbers.value: 89% full; 64% w/o AST fragmentation; 60% w/o cross-file RAG; 77% w/o PoV guidance

structure_gain: w/o cross-file RAG (single-function context only) drops F1 from 89% to 60% (-29pp); w/o AST-based fragmentation drops F1 to 64% (-25pp); w/o PoV-guided reasoning drops F1 to 77% (-12pp), all on the same 57-project dataset
confound_note: Each ablation arm removes one mechanism (AST fragmentation, multi-agent cross-file RAG, or PoV guidance) on the same dataset, isolating that component's contribution reasonably cleanly, though underlying LLM/agent budget per arm is not explicitly confirmed identical
threats_to_datum: Ground truth relies on only two human annotators; PoV-guided reasoning applicable to only ~51% of vulnerabilities that have available PoV tests (Sec 6 Threats to Validity)

title: ZeroFalse: Improving Precision in Static Analysis with LLMs

key_numbers.metric: F1 gain, optimized vs minimal-context prompt (OpenVuln)

structure_gain: Optimized vs minimal-context prompt: average F1 +0.176 across 10 models (OpenVuln, Table 4), same models.
confound_note: Baseline-prompt vs optimized-prompt comparison holds the LLM and decoding (temperature=0, schema-constrained JSON) fixed and varies only the structured context content (taint trace + CWE rubric vs minimal alert text)
threats_to_datum: gemini-2.5-pro F1 drops from 0.91 on synthetic OWASP to 0.37 on real-world OpenVuln, suggesting possible benchmark-specific overfitting (Threats to Validity)

title: MulVul: Retrieval-augmented Multi-Agent Code Vulnerability Detection via Cross-Model Prompt Evolution

key_numbers.value: MulVul 34.79% vs GPT-4o 3.86% vs LLM x CPG 24.58% vs LLMVulExp 22.72% vs VISION 18.12%

structure_gain: Removing retrieval: Macro-F1 34.56% -> 21.80% (-12.76pp), same model (the -30.70 figure belongs to the GPT-4o baseline row).
confound_note: Main SOTA comparison (Table 2, vs GPT-4o/LLM x CPG/LLMVulExp/VISION) changes architecture, model, and representation simultaneously; only the internal Table 4 ablation isolates retrieval while holding agents/LLM fixed.
threats_to_datum: Evaluated only on PrimeVul (C/C++); authors themselves flag generalizability to other languages as unexplored; numbers from a v1 arXiv preprint, not yet peer reviewed; one baseline (LLM x CPG) is itself GNN-assisted, complicating a like-for-like comparison.

title: How Code Representation Shapes False-Positive Dynamics in Cross-Language LLM Vulnerability Detection

key_numbers.metric: FPR escalation with text fine-tuning (Qwen3-8B, OWASP Java)
key_numbers.value: 0.763 zero-shot -> 0.866 pilot -> 1.000 full-scale, while F1 stays 0.637-0.688

key_numbers.metric: FPR reduction switching text-trained model's input to AST, no retraining (Qwen3-8B)

key_numbers.value: FPR reduction of Delta=-0.527 under text->AST switch

structure_gain: Switching a text-fine-tuned model's inference-time input from raw text to pruned AST (no retraining) cuts FPR by 0.282-0.527 depending on CWE, with only a modest F1 cost (e.g. 0.688->0.637 for Qwen3-8B), same model weights and training budget -- a pure representation-only manipulation
confound_note: Full factorial design fixes the base model and LoRA training budget while independently varying training-time representation (text/AST) and inference-time representation (text/AST), including a cross-representation probe that isolates representation from training adaptation
threats_to_datum: Restricted to intra-procedural code units by design; only two 8B models and two target languages tested; ~9.9% of BenchmarkPython samples excluded for being AST-unparseable, a potential selection bias (Limitations)

title: Antaeus: Hunting Repository-Level Logic Vulnerabilities via Context-Grounded LLM Reasoning

key_numbers.value: Claude: 15 vs 9 vs 9; GPT: 12 vs 8 vs 7

structure_gain: Removing either context source (local callee augmentation or repository-context bundle) roughly halves true-positive detections (Claude: 15->9/9; GPT: 12->8/7) at fixed LLM backbone (Table IV), directly isolating representation contribution.
confound_note: Table IV ablation holds the LLM backbone fixed (separately for Claude and GPT) and toggles context components (local augmentation, repo bundle) individually, a clean representation-only comparison; Table III's comparison to function-level and agentic baselines instead varies approach and context together.
threats_to_datum: Self-reported: depth-one call-graph expansion may miss deeper interprocedural evidence, LLM sink identification can be incomplete or spurious, prioritization heuristic is imperfect and unproven optimal, small evaluation set (28 CVEs, 2 CWE types) may not generalize across languages or proprietary code (Section V).
